page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, the instance supplies 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features a 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX Tile, AMX INT8, and Intel Deep Learning Boost (VNNI). The VM includes 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM configuration of 4.0 GB per core. It contains no attached local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage disks for persistent I/O.

Benchmark evaluations show competitive throughput in data transformation tasks. The instance reaches top-tier single-threaded compression performance, scoring 36.55 GB/sec in gzip compression and 15.22 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In lightweight AI workloads, text generation for a 135M parameter language model performs in the upper quartile at 271.19 tokens/sec. Across wider stress-ng workloads, general PassMark CPU metrics, Redis key-value operations (16.48 million ops/sec), and static web delivery (17.16 GB/sec), performance remains consistent with standard mid-tier general-purpose averages.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v7 delivers balanced compute and memory density without the premium overhead associated with specialized accelerator hardware or high-ratio memory nodes. The absence of bundled local NVMe storage means storage costs scale separately via remote volumes, which trade raw local disk IOPS for disk mobility and persistence. The hardware profile is appropriate for medium-sized relational databases, Redis in-memory caching nodes, enterprise web applications, data ingestion pipelines, and lightweight CPU-bound inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, backed by 32.0 GB of memory and a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V using the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512. It contains no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote Premium Storage attachments. In performance testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-threaded data compression alongside solid mid-range compute, memory bandwidth, and Redis caching throughput. The balanced resource allocation makes it well positioned for enterprise web serving, relational databases, data preprocessing, and small-model language inference.
